NoteTexAccessor::input_tags¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::input_tags() const

Turn External-Input Directives Into Visible Tags¶

input_tags() replaces complete \input{path} and \include{path} commands with the plain-text marker [include:path]. It exists for workflows that need to retain the fact and target of an external source reference while making the cell self-contained and safe to display without resolving files.

The method does not read the filesystem, search TeX paths, append an extension, or splice another document into the Note. Its old expansion-shaped name was therefore inaccurate. Use includes() when paths should be extracted as a ragged result instead of embedded back into the source text.

Whitespace between the command and its required braced argument is accepted. Balanced braces inside the path are retained. A malformed directive without a complete braced argument remains unchanged. A doubled backslash is a TeX linebreak boundary, so \\input{literal} is not mistaken for an input command. Other commands, surrounding prose, and cell order are preserved byte for byte.

The operation is lane-wise and shape preserving for scalar, vector, matrix, and rank-three Notes. It allocates a new Text Note and does not mutate the receiver. Undefined input remains undefined; non-text dtypes are rejected. The scanner is linear in source bytes and reserves output capacity from the input size.

Example 1: Both Directive Spellings¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(Before \input{chapters/one} after)",
    R"(\include {appendix})"});
std::cout << source.tex().input_tags() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Before [include:chapters/one] after", "[include:appendix]"]

Example 2: Escaped And Malformed Boundaries¶

const auto boundaries = pluss::make_note(
    {R"(\\input{literal})", R"(\input broken)", R"(\input{nested/{part}})"});
std::cout << boundaries.tex().input_tags() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\\\input{literal}", "\\input broken", "[include:nested/{part}]"]

Example 3: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(Before \input{chapters/one} after)",
                             R"(\include {appendix} and \\input{literal})",
                             R"(\input{nested/{part}})", R"(\input broken)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto tagged = grid.tex().input_tags();
std::cout << tagged << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << tagged.sizes()[0] << ", " << tagged.sizes()[1]
          << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Before [include:chapters/one] after", "[include:appendix] and \\\\input{literal}"], 
  ["[include:nested/{part}]", "\\input broken"]
]
shape=[2, 2]

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().input_tags().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().input_tags();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "input tags Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
input tags Int64: rejected
